title: Finite-projective summand equations
statement:
For a finite projective $F^r$ and a displayed splitting $(i_r,p_r)$, the
arrows $\pi_{h,E,F^r}$ and $\rho_{F^r}$ are inverse and are independent of
the chosen finite-free summand presentation.

proof.text: Use the ringed-topos data $h:(\mathcal T,S)\to(\mathcal S,R)$ and $E\in D(S)$ of the arrow definition; regard each coefficient sheaf as a complex in degree zero. Write $A(X)=Rh_*E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}X$ and $B(X)=Rh_*(E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*X)$. Let $\alpha_X:Lh^*A(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Rh_*E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*X$ be the canonical comparison and $c_X=(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\alpha_X$, whose adjunct is $\pi_X$. For any coefficient map $u:X\to Y$, naturality in the second variable of the cited derived tensor comparison gives $\alpha_Y Lh^*A(u)=(1\otimes Lh^*u)\alpha_X$. Tensor functoriality then gives $c_Y Lh^*A(u)=(1_E\otimes Lh^*u)c_X$. Under the natural Hom bijection of the derived adjunction specified in the arrow definition, the adjuncts of the two sides are $\pi_Y A(u)$ and $B(u)\pi_X$, respectively; hence these maps are equal. Taking $u=i_r:F^r\to R^{\oplus N_r}$ and $u=p_r:R^{\oplus N_r}\to F^r$ gives $B(i_r)\pi_{F^r}=\pi_{N_r}A(i_r)$ and $B(p_r)\pi_{N_r}=\pi_{F^r}A(p_r)$.

The splitting has $p_ri_r=1$. Specializing the finite-free lemma to $\Lambda=R$, $N=N_r$ and shift $a=0$, use its two inverse identities, compute $\rho_{F^r}\pi_{F^r}=A(p_r)\rho_rB(i_r)\pi_{F^r}=A(p_r)\rho_r\pi_rA(i_r)=A(p_ri_r)=1$. For the other composite, compute $\pi_{F^r}\rho_{F^r}=\pi_{F^r}A(p_r)\rho_rB(i_r)=B(p_r)\pi_r\rho_rB(i_r)=B(p_ri_r)=1$. Thus the displayed maps are inverse.

The map $\pi_{F^r}$ is intrinsic because its defining adjunct $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\alpha_{F^r}$ does not use a splitting. For any second displayed finite-free summand presentation, repeat Steps 1 and 2 with its inclusion, projection and rank to obtain a map $\rho'_{F^r}$ satisfying both inverse equations for this same $\pi_{F^r}$. Then $\rho'_{F^r}=\rho'_{F^r}(\pi_{F^r}\rho_{F^r})=(\rho'_{F^r}\pi_{F^r})\rho_{F^r}=\rho_{F^r}$. This proves independence of the inverse and of the intrinsic forward arrow.
